### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via automation.execute (sdk, the route ledger binds it to POST /automation/:ns/:name/trigger), automation.listRuns (sdk, the route ledger binds it to GET /automation/:ns/:name/runs), automation.trigger (sdk, the route ledger binds it to POST /automation/trigger/:ns/:name), listRuns (sdk, the bare tail of client method automation.listRuns, bound to GET /automation/:ns/:name/runs), /automation/:ns/:name/trigger (route, a path literal in createDispatcherPlugin), /automation/trigger/:ns/:name (route, a path literal in createDispatcherPlugin))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via automation.execute (sdk, the route ledger binds it to POST /automation/:ns/:name/trigger), listRuns (sdk, the bare tail of client method automation.listRuns, bound to GET /automation/:ns/:name/runs))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via listRuns (sdk, the bare tail of client method automation.listRuns, bound to GET /automation/:ns/:name/runs))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **30** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cd4012f47443d158ccc55c6456dfa5232312f589` — the merge of head `398268290209d2cec7309faa94c8b2221b9a2551` into base `895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cd4012f47443d158ccc55c6456dfa5232312f589 && git checkout cd4012f47443d158ccc55c6456dfa5232312f589
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87 398268290209d2cec7309faa94c8b2221b9a2551 && git checkout -B drift-repro 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87 && git merge --no-ff 398268290209d2cec7309faa94c8b2221b9a2551

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Review — PASS

Head-sha: `398268290209d2cec7309faa94c8b2221b9a2551`
Reviewer: review-c (areas S5 + S6) · read 2026-11-15T14:29Z
Implemented-by: `claude/area-A5b-33026` (S6 session_01QsR2jUZKdq3PK2Sab53cT3) · Reviewed-by: session_01QsR2jRMKz5NhWVrE4E1U5x

Read at the head: the net diff against its merge base (3 files, +73/-0; the `42667cd1`/`36d24369` pair nets to zero and the merge is a squash), card #33026 in full, and `dispatcher-plugin.ts` around the declarations (`domainDecidesEveryVerb`, the fallback seam, `addressedAutomationRoutes`).

1. **Premise and fix.** The card's mechanism holds on `main`: only the two-segment `/automation` patterns and `:name/runs` were declared, so the three addressed mounts fell through to the transport's 405. The three new declarations name exactly the registered addressed mounts, with the same verb and spelling: `get /automation/:ns/:name/runs`, `post /automation/:ns/:name/trigger`, `post /automation/trigger/:ns/:name`. A declaration only feeds the fallback seam, which receives a request only after the router could not route it (`resolveMountedRoute` decides membership). So no served route is shadowed, and the CONTROLs (served `POST` on both trigger shapes still runs) pin that.
2. **Scope complete.** The other addressed mounts (`toggle`, `clone`, `runs/:runId…`, connector `connection`) have bare counterparts that are not declared either, so there is no bare/addressed split left for them. The card names exactly these three.
3. **Pins.** The five new rows reproduce the card's steps 2–3 (DELETE/POST/PUT on `/runs`, GET on both triggers) through the Hono socket, and each reads the door off the body (the dispatcher envelope, not the transport's `details`). The no-namespace CONTROL pins the 404 the changeset names. Ablations are in the reports (14/4/4 red, one per declaration).
4. **Clause-② no / Metadata-protocol none: right.** No accept-set or schema moves. A refused request is still refused; only which door answers changes (the domain's 405/401 in place of the transport's 405). The anonymous caller now gets 401 ahead of 405, the same as the bare path. Patch changeset on `@objectstack/runtime`. Each sentence was checked against the diff and the card: the bare answer (`405`, `Allow: GET`, `401` anonymous), the addressed answer before (`Allow: GET, HEAD`, `error.details`), the list of verbs, the answer after (`Allow: GET` for `/runs`, `Allow: POST` for both triggers), "A served verb on an address … unchanged", and the no-namespace 404. All true.
5. **Gates not judged.** At review time 14 succeeded, 16 were skipped and 18 were in progress, with none red. The scoped re-check on the merge head is NOT MEASURED (verify-lock timeout), as the report says; CI's check-runs stand in for it. Landing needs every check green on this head.

No must-fix, no should-fix.
